sentences.text:
The applicant has filed this application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for enlarging the applicant on Regular Bail in connection with FIR being C.R.
No.11196002240204/2024 registered with Bapod Police Station, Vadodara City, for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(N) of the IPC and Section 3(A), 4, 5(L), 5(J)(2) of the POCSO Act.

4. Learned advocate for the applicant would submit that considering the role attributed to the applicant and nature of allegation levelled, the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21183/2025 ORDER DATED: 04/12/2025 undefined applicant may be enlarged on regular bail.
It is submitted that since the charge-sheet is filed, no useful purpose would be served by keeping the applicant in jail for indefinite period.
It is further contended that the applicant is ready and willing to abide by all the conditions that may be imposed by this Court, if released on bail.
5. As against the same, learned APP appearing for the respondent - State has vehemently objected to the grant of regular bail.

Learned APP has submitted that looking to the nature of offence and the role attributed to the present applicant as coming out from the charge-sheet, this Court may not exercise the discretion in favour of the applicant and the application may be dismissed.
6. Learned Advocates for the parties do not press for reasoned order.
7. I have heard learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers.
Following aspects are considered:-

(i) While the fact of the victim being around 15 years and 3 months at the time of incident, could not be overlooked, yet it would appear that at the time of incident, the applicant was also aged around 24/25 years

(ii) It also appears that the applicant and the victim belong to the same community and whereas the applicant and the victim had resided for more than a year together and whereas during such period, the victim had also given birth child of the applicant.
Thus, pointing out a relationship between the paries and negating any allegation of there being any threat, coercion or intimidation in the relationship.
(iii) The fact of the applicant being in custody since 18.05.2025 and the charge-sheet having been laid.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21183/2025 ORDER DATED: 04/12/2025 undefined (iv) Fact that there being no antecedents against the present applicant.

This Court has taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40.

sentences.text: In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of the allegations made in the First Information Report, without discussing the evidence in detail, prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.
9. Hence, the present application is allowed.
If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Court concerned will be free to take appropriate action in the matter.
11. Bail bond to be executed before the lower Court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions in accordance with law.

12. At the stage of trial, the trial court shall not be influenced by any observations of this Court which are of preliminary nature made at this stage, only for the purpose of considering the application of the applicant for being released on regular bail.
13. The application is allowed in the aforesaid terms.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.

(e) not to enter Vadodara City till the deposition of the prosecutrix is over in the trial except for making of presence and attending the trial;
[f] mark presence once a week before the concerned Police Station for a period of six months;
